subject: Acme Corp POC: success criteria & eval plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Discovery — POC next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya — great to meet you both on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the POC scope and evaluation approach: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Goal: Reduce time-to-insight on customer support cases using an LLM-powered triage assistant (target: 40% reduction in average handling time).
- Primary success metrics: avg handle time (AHT), triage accuracy (match to human tags), false-positive rate on escalation.
- Timeline: 4-week POC (start: Jun 8) with a short shadow period then an online trial on a subset of traffic.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Week 0 (prep): access + data sample exchange, environment access (VPC/IP allowlist), sign mutual action plan.
2) Week 1: offline evals on representative dataset; baseline comparisons and rubric grading.
3) Week 2: shadow mode (non-blocking, live traffic) to measure latency and behavior.
4) Week 3: targeted online trial on 10% traffic with rollback plan.
5) Week 4: analysis, handoff, and recommendations.

Action items / owners:
- Acme: provide a 2k-sample of annotated tickets + access list (Priya) — due Jun 5.
- Redwood (me): send POC scope doc and mutual action plan — attached.
- Redwood (Dylan + Rachel): propose eval methodology (offline rubric + shadow metrics) and tuning plan — will follow up in-thread.

Attachments: acme_poc_scope.pdf, mutual_action_plan.docx

Are you OK with the plan and timeline? If yes, we’ll lock resources and schedule a kickoff for Jun 8.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

1) Success metrics — can you confirm how you calculate triage accuracy? We want precision on urgent escalations to be prioritized over recall.
2) Offline evals — do you have a suggested grading rubric we can review before sharing the sample?
3) Data security — we’ll need a short description of where traffic will run during the shadow and online phases (hosted vs dedicated). Can Dylan advise?

We can deliver the 2k-sample by EOD Jun 5. Kickoff Jun 8 works for the product + infra folks.

Regards,

Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acme.com

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Discovery — POC next steps

Jordan — great questions. Quick answers inline, and I’ll let Dylan + Rachel add technical detail on security and evals.

1) Triage accuracy: our standard is token-level/intent-level matching depending on your tagging scheme; for urgent escalations we can report precision@k and produce a separate metric focused on escalation precision (to match your priority).

2) Rubric: attaching a draft eval rubric (acme_eval_rubric.xlsx) — it includes labels, grading scale (0–3), and examples. Rachel, could you confirm whether a 0–3 rubric is sufficient for Acme’s reviewers?

3) Data security: Dylan — can you add a short note on where inference will run for shadow vs online (hosted vs Dedicated) and any IP allowlist/VPC requirements?

If that all sounds good, we’ll finalize the MAP and send a DocuSign link for signatures.

Thanks — Marissa

Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:42:00 -0700

Hi all — short security/ops note: 
- Shadow mode will run on Redwood Hosted in a non-blocking read-only configuration (no writes to your production systems). Traffic is proxied and sampled; logs are retained per the MAP. For customers requiring network isolation we can run in Dedicated (VPC) during the shadow/online phases — that requires firewall rules and an IP allowlist (we’ll provide CIDR ranges).
- For the online 10% trial, we recommend Dedicated if you plan to send any production traffic that could contain PII; otherwise hosted with redaction is fine for initial tests.

I’ll prepare a short ops checklist and a minimal runbook for the kickoff.

-Dylan
Principal Engineer, Solutions 
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intro / Discovery — POC next steps (eval methodology)

Thanks — adding detail on the evaluation methodology so we’re aligned before Acme shares the sample: 

Proposed eval approach:
A) Offline evals (Week 1):
- Use the 2k annotated tickets to run offline scoring. For each example we’ll compute:
  - Label match score (0–3): 3=exact match to human tag; 2=acceptable alternate tag; 1=partial; 0=incorrect/harmful.
  - Escalation precision: does the model flag an urgent ticket that a human would escalate? (binary/precision focus).
  - Latency estimate on representative sequence lengths.
- Deliverable: offline report with per-case grading and aggregated metrics, plus examples where model and human disagree for error analysis.

B) Shadow (Week 2):
- Run on sampled live traffic (non-blocking). Collect model outputs, timestamps, routing decisions, and compare with historical human tags where available.
- Metrics: live precision/false-positive for escalations, distribution drift vs offline sample, and stability of top-k suggestions.

C) Online trial (Week 3):
- 10% live traffic with monitoring and rollback. Key ops metrics: latency p95, error rate, and business impact proxies (AHT change).

Rubric notes:
- 0–3 is recommended for faster labeling and clearer inter-rater reliability. We’ll include concrete examples in the rubric sheet.
- We recommend 2–3 internal reviewers from Acme for spot checks to calibrate labeling.

I attached the draft rubric (acme_eval_rubric.xlsx). If you want, we can run a 30-min rubric calibration session during the kickoff.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
